title: Best 30-Pint Dehumidifier (2026): Rooms Up to 1,500 Sq Ft
h1: The Best 30-Pint Dehumidifiers for Bedrooms, Offices and Small Spaces
dek: The middle size most rooms actually need — once you decode what "30 pints" means under today's test rules.
description: The best 30-pint dehumidifier for 2026, for bedrooms, offices and small apartments, with DOE 2019 ratings decoded plus Honeywell, GE and Frigidaire notes.
intro: A **30-pint dehumidifier** is the size most people actually need. A bedroom, home office, single-car garage or small apartment doesn't call for a big 50-pint machine — and paying for capacity you won't use mostly buys you a bigger box and a louder fan.

The label is confusing, though. In 2019 the Department of Energy changed its test so that dehumidifiers are rated at 65°F instead of 80°F. Cooler air holds less water, so the same hardware now earns a lower number: many units still sold as "30-pint" carry a current rating of about **22 pints**. That's not a downgrade — it's the same machine measured more realistically. Below are the models in this class worth buying, plus one honestly labeled modern alternative.
topPicksLead: The **hOmeLabs HME020030N** is our top 30-pint pick for most bedrooms, offices and small apartments: honestly rated, ENERGY STAR certified and equipped with auto-defrost for cooler rooms.

blocks.text: The test change lowered published capacities across the board by roughly 30%. When you compare models, make sure you're comparing old-scale numbers with old-scale numbers, or current with current.

We don't run a test lab. We compared DOE 2019 ratings wherever manufacturers publish them, ENERGY STAR listings, manuals and spec sheets for coverage, tank size, drainage and defrost, plus manufacturer-published noise and power figures. We then read owner reviews for recurring issues like leaky buckets, short lifespans and humidistats that read far off.
We favored units that are honest about their current rating, include auto-defrost and offer a hose connection, since a small bucket is the biggest day-to-day annoyance in this class.

sections.heading: What to look for in a 30-pint dehumidifier

items.label: The DOE 2019 rating
items.text: Check the spec sheet for the current number. About 20–22 pints is the honest equivalent of an old "30-pint" label.

items.label: Match to dampness, not just square feet
items.text: A musty bedroom or office is a good fit. A wet space needs more capacity regardless of size — see our [size guide](/guides/dehumidifier-size-guide/).

items.label: Tank size or a hose
items.text: Most units in this class hold only a few pints. If the room stays damp, a continuous-drain hose saves a lot of trips.

items.label: Auto-defrost
items.text: Essential if the unit will run in a cool basement, garage or closet below the mid-60s.

items.label: Published noise figures
items.text: In a bedroom or office, look for decibel numbers on the spec sheet rather than marketing adjectives.

blocks.text: Is a 30-pint dehumidifier enough for a basement?

For a small basement that's musty rather than wet, often yes — especially under about 1,000 square feet. For a larger or genuinely damp basement, size up to our [50-pint picks](/best/best-50-pint-dehumidifier/) or the [basement guide](/best/best-dehumidifier-for-basement/).

Honeywell sells 30-pint-class models, including the TP30AWKN and a smart Wi-Fi ENERGY STAR version with app control. They're reasonable alternatives to our picks — check the current DOE rating and whether the model you're looking at includes a hose connection. Our [Honeywell guide](/best/best-honeywell-dehumidifier/) covers the lineup.

GE, Waykar and Kenmore all sell dehumidifiers in this size range. Judge them by the same checklist: honest DOE 2019 rating, auto-defrost, a drain connection and published noise figures. See our [GE](/best/best-ge-dehumidifier/) and [Waykar](/best/best-waykar-dehumidifier/) guides for specific models.

The FAD301NUD is an earlier version of Frigidaire's 30-pint design. If you find one, check its model number against the CPSC recall database and confirm the warranty terms before buying; otherwise the current FAD301NWD is the one to look for.

The **hOmeLabs HME020030N** is the best 30-pint dehumidifier for most bedrooms, offices and small apartments. Choose the **Frigidaire FAD301NWD** for hands-off continuous draining, the **TOSOT GDN30AZ** when quiet matters most, and the **Vremi 30-Pint** to spend the least. If you'd rather skip the old-scale labels entirely, the **Midea Cube 20** is honestly rated and the most efficient option here.

faqs.a: The hOmeLabs HME020030N for most rooms: about 22 pints a day under the current DOE test, ENERGY STAR certified and equipped with auto-defrost. The Frigidaire FAD301NWD is best for continuous draining and the TOSOT GDN30AZ for quiet.

faqs.q: What does "30-pint" mean under the 2019 DOE rating?
faqs.a: Most units branded "30-pint" are named after the older test standard. Under the 2019 test, run at 65°F instead of 80°F, the same hardware is rated at roughly 22 pints. The machine is the same; only the number changed.

faqs.q: What size room is a 30-pint dehumidifier good for?
faqs.a: Roughly up to 1,500 square feet of damp space: a bedroom, home office, single-car garage, large closet or small apartment.

faqs.q: Is a Honeywell 30-pint smart dehumidifier worth it?
faqs.a: It can be if you value app control and remote humidity readings. Compare its current DOE rating, drain options and warranty against non-smart models, which often cost less for the same capacity.

faqs.q: Is a 30-pint dehumidifier enough for a basement?
faqs.a: For a small, musty basement, often yes. For a larger or actively wet basement, a 50-pint unit is the better choice.

faqs.q: What's the difference between a 30-pint and a 50-pint dehumidifier?
faqs.a: A 50-pint unit removes more than twice as much water under the current DOE test and covers much larger, damper spaces, but it's bigger, louder and more expensive. Don't oversize for a bedroom or office.
